name: cubrik
description: Use your cubrik account from any MCP client: create, test, start and pause AI trading agents that run on the brokers and exchanges connected to cubrik (Binance, OKX, Hyperliquid, MetaTrader and others); backtest rule-based ideas on historical candles; read balances, open positions, closed trades, results and Analytics advice; copy ready-made agents from cubrik's Library; and place, change and close orders through each connected platform's own tools (named <platform>_<tool>). 40 tools plus each platform's own, and five prompts. Hosted remote server: sign in through your MCP client (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE) and choose what it may do: read, manage agents, trade. No API key; broker keys stay in cubrik, and no tool deposits, withdraws or transfers funds. Comes with cubrik's Intermediate plan and above (paid). Not investment advice.

http.description: Hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server. Your MCP client discovers the OAuth 2.1 metadata and opens cubrik's sign-in, where you choose what it may do (read, manage agents, trade); no API key is needed.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The cubrik account's plan and what is left of it: credits this month and when they renew, active agents and the limit, the schedules agents may run on, and which connected platforms agents can use.

tools.name: list_platforms
tools.description: The brokers and exchanges connected to the cubrik account: each one's id, status, whether agents can use it, and its last known balance. One marked demo is cubrik's Demo account, with virtual money.

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: Balances and open positions on every platform connected to cubrik, read from the platforms themselves.

tools.name: get_trade_history
tools.description: Closed trades on the connected platforms, newest first: instrument, side, size, prices, profit or loss, and the agent that opened the trade when one did.

tools.name: get_trading_results
tools.description: What the account made or lost on its connected platforms over a period: profit and loss, number of trades, win rate, and the split by agent and by account.

tools.name: connect_platform
tools.description: The platforms cubrik lists, and the link to the page in cubrik where a broker or exchange is connected. Keys and sign-ins are entered there, never in the chat.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: Every agent on the account: id, name, status (active or paused), schedule, whether it may trade, and when it runs next.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: One agent in full: its instruction or backtest rules, schedule, platforms, limits, what its runs cost in credits, and its performance.

tools.name: get_agent_runs
tools.description: An agent's most recent runs, or one run by id: how each ended, what it found and did, the trades it placed and the credits it used.

tools.name: list_agent_templates
tools.description: Ready-made agent setups: each template's name, what it does, its schedule and its instruction.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Creates an agent and its schedule from an instruction, or from a backtest so that it runs those rules exactly as tested. It is created paused and does nothing until it is started.

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description: Changes an agent's name, schedule, instruction or backtest rules, its platforms or limits. A paused agent stays paused.

tools.name: start_agent
tools.description: Starts a paused agent on its schedule, optionally with a first run now. An agent allowed to trade places orders on its platform from then on.

tools.name: pause_agent
tools.description: Pauses an agent until it is started again or until a given time. Positions stay open on the platform.

tools.name: pause_all_agents
tools.description: Pauses every active agent on the account at once. Open positions stay open on the platforms.

tools.name: test_agent
tools.description: A dry run of an agent now: it decides as on a real run but places nothing, and says what it would have done. Costs no credits.

tools.name: run_agent_now
tools.description: A real run of an agent now, outside its schedule. An agent allowed to trade may place orders. Uses credits.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description: Deletes an agent. It stops at once; positions it opened stay open on the platform.

tools.name: run_backtest
tools.description: Backtests a trading idea's rules on historical candles (markets, timeframe, entry and exit conditions, stop, target, risk per trade, leverage, or a regular buy) in the background. Changes nothing on any account.

tools.name: get_backtest
tools.description: A backtest by id: status and progress, then the simulated return, maximum drawdown, win rate, number of trades and the assumptions behind them.

tools.name: check_rules_now
tools.description: Whether a saved strategy's entry and exit rules are true on the latest candles, per symbol.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: cubrik's Library of ready-made agents, backtested every week: each one's name, markets, style, return, drawdown and score, narrowed by name, market or style.

tools.name: get_library_agent
tools.description: One Library agent in full: its instruction, markets, schedule and weekly backtest history.

tools.name: copy_library_agent
tools.description: Copies a Library agent into the account as a new agent, paused.

tools.name: get_analysis
tools.description: The Analytics report of one connected platform over a period: profit and loss, trades, win rate, best and worst markets, and the split by agent and by market.

tools.name: get_advice
tools.description: Analytics' advice for the agents trading on one platform: what to change in each agent, why, and what it is expected to change.

tools.name: apply_advice
tools.description: Writes one piece of Analytics advice onto its agent, changing that agent's rules.

tools.name: get_price
tools.description: Latest price and 24-hour change for up to eight instruments.

tools.name: get_candles
tools.description: OHLCV candles for one instrument and timeframe.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: Instruments cubrik has prices for (crypto pairs, forex, indices, commodities and stocks), searched by ticker or name.

tools.name: get_news
tools.description: Recent market headlines, filtered for their likely impact, optionally narrowed to instruments.

tools.name: get_economic_calendar
tools.description: Upcoming economic events (rate decisions, inflation and jobs prints, auctions) with their expected impact.

tools.name: get_market_overview
tools.description: The main markets' moves, the biggest movers and the market's overall state.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: The account's recent notifications (agent results, risk alerts, finished backtests), newest first.

tools.name: mark_notifications_read
tools.description: Marks the given notifications, or all of them, as read.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: The messages of one cubrik conversation, such as the thread an agent writes its runs into.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: The account's cubrik skills: playbooks the person wrote for cubrik's chat and agents, and where each is switched on.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: One cubrik skill in full, by name: its description and its instructions.

tools.name: save_skill
tools.description: Creates a cubrik skill, or replaces the one with the same name, and sets whether cubrik's chat and which agents use it.

tools.name: delete_skill
tools.description: Deletes one of the account's cubrik skills by name.

prompts.name: daily_brief
prompts.description: How the account stands this morning: balances and open positions, what the agents did overnight, and what is on today's economic calendar.

prompts.name: new_agent
prompts.description: Turns a trading idea into rules, backtests them, and sets the idea up as an agent.

arguments.name: idea
arguments.description: The trading idea, in your own words.

prompts.name: backtest_idea
prompts.description: Writes an idea as rules and backtests it on historical candles.

prompts.name: weekly_review
prompts.description: How the agents did this week, what Analytics advises changing, and which advice is worth applying.

prompts.name: emergency_stop
prompts.description: Pauses every agent at once and lists the positions still open.

examples.title: Portfolio
examples.description: Balances, open positions and this month's result
examples.prompt: Show my balances and open positions on every platform, and how much I made this month.

examples.title: Backtest an idea
examples.description: Rules run on historical candles; nothing changes on any account
examples.prompt: Backtest this on BTC 4h over the last year: buy when RSI goes under 30 and the price is above the 200 EMA, with a 2% stop and a 4% target.

examples.title: Copy from the Library
examples.description: A ready-made agent copied into the account, paused
examples.prompt: Find a Library agent for gold with a drawdown under 15% and copy it to my account.

examples.title: Agent from a backtest
examples.description: Created paused, then a dry run that places nothing
examples.prompt: Create an agent from that backtest, test it, and tell me what it would do right now.

examples.title: Weekly review
examples.description: Results, Analytics and its advice per agent
examples.prompt: How did my agents do this week, and what does Analytics advise changing?

examples.title: Pause everything
examples.description: Every agent paused at once; open positions stay open
